title: National AI in Work Day and how I use AI tools at my job
dek: September 30 is National AI in Work Day, and I am thinking about how to use AI tools at work in a way that actually helps.
body: For those of you starting an early shift, today is National AI in Work Day. It focuses on using AI responsibly in the workplace to help people do their jobs well, and it arrives at a time when a lot of us are figuring that out as we go.

In my own work, AI tools are most helpful with the small, repetitive tasks. They can help me summarize a long document, draft a first version of a routine email, or organize my notes after a meeting. That leaves me more time for the parts of the job that need my full attention.

I have also learned to be careful. I read everything before I send it, I check facts myself, and I do not paste private information into a tool unless my workplace has said it is allowed. When something important is on the line, I want my own judgment in charge.

I think the best approach is to treat these tools like a helpful new coworker. They are fast and eager, but they still need clear instructions and someone to review their work. Being honest with your team about when you used them helps build trust too.
Today, try using an AI tool for one small task you usually dread, then review the result closely. You will learn quickly where it saves you time and where you still need to do it yourself.
